Death Reference No. 48 of 2010

MA Mannan Mohon DAG with Md Aminur Rahman Chowdhury and Kazi Bazlur Rashid, AAGs-For the State.

full_judgment:
10. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate of the appellant-condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani the learned Deputy Attorney General controverted the argument advanced from the side of the defence and opposing the grounds of the appeal submits that, it is not the case of the defence that the UD case being No. 33 of 2006 was not filed by the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani rather he admitted it and it is clear from the contents of the application of Jail Appeal and from the attending circumstances of the case that the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani immediately after the occurrence; on the following day of death i.e. on 29-11- 2006 going to the concerned police station lodged the UD case to misdirect the actual cause of death and to hide him from the heinous offence of the killing his wife by injecting her the insecticide poison. The learned Deputy Attorney General hereinafter DAG further submits that it is apparent from the face of the record that the story of snake-bite is a downright-false as after examination of the viscera by Expert it has come to the limelight that for injecting insecticide poison in the body, the deceased Sirina Khatun died. The learned DAG in this context; specifically asserted that the chemical examiner vide his Report dated 27-3-2007(Exhibit-4) after examination of viscera clearly opined that in the viscera there is on existence of কার্বামেটস (কীটনাশক) বিষ।” learned DAG during his submissions also submits, despite; the date of occurrence of this case is 28-11-2006 at about 11-00 PM and the formal ejahar was lodged on 18-1-2008 nevertheless; there is no doubt as to why this unusual delay in lodging the ejahar occurred. It is from the body of the ejahar itself which has been marked as Exhibit-1 that the husband of the deceased Shirina on the following day i.e. on 29-11-2006 informed the local police station with regard to the death of his wife on which a UD case being No. 33 of 2006 was started. The reason which was Cited within the contents of the UD case was investigated by the concerned Kahalu police station of Bogra district and after completion of investigation the investigating authority submitted their final report as to the falsities of the UD case No. 33 of 2006 and after the end of UD case filed by the husband of the deceased the informant lodged the regular ejahar on which Kahalu police station Case No. 12 dated 18-1-2008 was started against the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani under sections 302/201/ 34 of the Penal Code. Therefore, obviously the reason is clear as to why the delay was occurred. The learned DAG also submits that initially the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani instituted a Jail Appeal through Jail Authority which was 236/2010 and it is not at all challenged or even denied from the side of the condemned-prisoner, in which he has specifically stated that his wife died by snake-bite. Subsequently; this jail appeal has been merged or amalgamated with the Criminal Appeal being No. 3239 of 2012. The learned DAG lastly submits that it is to be renumbered that the instant case is a wife killing case and the wife of the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani has been killed when she was under the exclusive control and custody of her husband the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani in his dwelling hut and the occurrence was held in dark night within their residence. Therefore, the established principle of law with regard to this; as to the responsibility or onus of proof is entirely lies upon the husband who is to explain alone as to why and how his wife met with her death. But in the instant case; nowhere any satisfactory or reasonable explanation or reason has been cited or given from the side of the condemned-prisoner as to the cause of death of his wife, rather; with an ill-motive to conceal the actual cause of death and to divert the reason for which his wife met with her death he informed the local inhabitants including the local police station that his wife died by snake-bite which is a downright false. The learned DAG.in support of his contention referred series of decisions of our Apex Court and of this Court. In the conclusion of the submissions the learned DAG submits that in a heinous way and with premeditation the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani by injecting insecticide poison to the person of his wife Shirina Khatun killed her brutally and it has been proved beyond all reasonable doubt from the side of the prosecution and considering all the evidence on records, facts and circumstances of the case the learned trial court scanning the evidence on record in it's true perspective decided the merit of the case in favour of the prosecution and against the defence and since the condemned-prisoner deserve highest punishment of this offence; there is no illegality or infirmity in passing the impugned judgment and order of conviction of sentence of death and as such the death reference is liable to be accepted and the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Bogra should be upheld. 

 37. Here in this case; as we have cited earlier elaborately that the husband Golam Rabbani has played a mysterious role to mislead the cause of death of his wife the deceased Shirina Khatun. The facts remains that the principle enunciated in a case of wife killing comes out from the provisions of section 106 of the Evidence Act wherein it is incorporated, when any fact, especially within the knowledge of any person, the burden of proving that fact is upon him. Definitely; section 106 of the Evidence Act has attribute the liability of proving the facts on the accused when the same especially within his knowledge. In this case; we have noticed that the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani and his wife the deceased Shirina Khatun while living in their residence the wife Shirina Khatun because of the poisonous reaction of insecticide poison in her body resulted her death, so the onus heavily and entirely lies on the husband as the fact is especially within the knowledge of the husband Golam Rabbani. Section 106 of the Evidence Act is very much clear in the said nature of fact. 

 40. In the forgoing narrative and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case we are of the unanimous view that the prosecution has been able to discharge their onus. Vis-a-vis; the burden of proof which was heavily lies upon the defence not at all discharged rather from the circumstantial evidence of this case it is proved that the deceased met with her death due to poisoning by her husband the condemned-prisoner Golam Rabbani. No doubt; the heinous offence as stated above was perpetrated by the condemned-prisorierin a pre- planned manner and the way of killing his wife Shirina is shocking to the. conscience of everybody and as such we find nothing in the facts and circumstances of the case especially on the above mentioned legal evidence of the case to interfere with the conviction and sentence which has been awarded by the trial court. The murder of Shirina Khatun is undoubtedly brutal, pre-planned and cool-planted and it appears that the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Bogra passed the death sentence against the condemned-prisoner in view of the brutality and gruesomeness, of the matter. In the facts and circumstances of the case accordingly; the learned trial Judge was perfectly justified in sentencing the condemned-prisoner-appellant to death. It is to be noticed here that we find nothing in the circumstances of the case in the context of the condemned-prisoner to take lenient view in the matter of the sentence despite our best concern to temper justice with mercy inasmuch as the condemned-prisoner deserve highest degree of penalty.
